recent_posts.title: Animated icons for React, without the setup pain
recent_posts.summary: @animateicons/react is a new npm package providing animated Lucide-style icons for React applications. It aims to simplify adding motion details to buttons, menus, dashboards, and landing pages without building custom SVG animations from scratch. Installation is via pnpm/npm and usage follows a straightforward named import pattern.

recent_posts.title: I Built a Studio Site That Scores 100 on Lighthouse — Here's What Actually Mattered
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares the key decisions behind building a studio/agency website that achieves a perfect 100 Lighthouse score. The three main factors highlighted are font optimization, use of React Server Components, and a counterintuitive hero section choice — demonstrating that good design and high performance can coexist.

recent_posts.title: Reuna Presenter - Multi-screen projection software for churches, in the browser
recent_posts.summary: Reuna Presenter is a browser-based presentation app for churches and live events, positioning itself as a web-native alternative to ProPresenter and EasyWorship. Built with Next.js 15, React 19, Supabase, and TypeScript in a Turborepo monorepo, it features multi-screen projection to congregation and stage monitors, a drag-and-drop service plan, a cloud-shared song library, Bible integration with offline support, mobile remote via QR code, container-query-based templates, MIDI timeline cues, and an interactive Screen Studio for managing physical outputs. The solo developer is offering 10 days of PRO access to church tech teams willing to test it in real Sunday services.

recent_posts.title: Pretext vs. Traditional Layout in 2026: Is the DOM Finally Obsolete?
recent_posts.summary: Pretext is a pure JavaScript text measurement library that performs layout calculations outside the browser's main rendering cycle, eliminating DOM reflows. It claims sub-millisecond layout performance with full i18n support. A community showcase called Pretext Wall demonstrates complex typographic effects like text flow around obstacles, shrink-wrap chat bubbles, and live line-by-line layout that would be impractical with traditional DOM methods. The post argues this approach may finally free web developers from the constraints of browser-native layout engines.

recent_posts.title: How I’m using AI to manage tasks, research, and notes in Notion
recent_posts.summary: A developer built Nityasha, an AI-powered personal assistant that integrates with Notion to automate task management, research, and note organization. The tool aims to solve common productivity pain points like buried tasks and time-consuming research by providing seamless Notion integration, automated research capabilities, simplified task prioritization, and instant image search functionality.

recent_posts.title: Static is boring — animate your icons 🎯
recent_posts.summary: AnimateIcons is a React library that transforms static SVG icons into smooth animations. It offers 45+ animated icons, works with React and Next.js, supports hover and programmatic control, and integrates with ShadCN CLI. The library aims to enhance user interfaces by adding purposeful motion to icons.

recent_posts.title: Adding GraphQL Flexibility to Your Existing APIs
recent_posts.summary: Modern applications use multiple API types (REST, gRPC, GraphQL) each with distinct advantages, but managing all three creates complexity and integration challenges. REST provides simple external interfaces, gRPC enables high-performance internal service communication, and GraphQL unifies client access while reducing endpoint coupling. Complete GraphQL migration is costly and risky, but Grafbase offers a solution to extend existing APIs with GraphQL capabilities without disrupting current systems.

recent_posts.title: Shadcn Form But with Tanstack Form as an Engine
recent_posts.summary: A developer created shadcn-tanstack-form, a library that combines shadcn/ui components with TanStack Form as the underlying form engine. The library provides drop-in replacement components that maintain the same API as vanilla shadcn forms while leveraging TanStack Form's capabilities. It includes pre-built form blocks for common use cases and can be installed via the shadcn CLI. The project is open source and the author plans to expand it with a universal form builder.
